questions.q: Why did Kristy Shen choose engineering over creative writing?
a: The math showed engineering would pay far more
Her parents insisted on the decision
She had already failed a writing course
It required no extra years of study
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes her comparing costs and salaries, then following the math.

questions.q: What does the summary call the worst kind of debt?
a: Consumer debt, because it carries the highest interest
A mortgage, because it lasts for decades
Student debt, because it grows over time
Business debt, because it is unpredictable
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls consumer debt worst because of its high interest rates.

questions.q: Why does Shen prefer spending on experiences rather than things?
a: The pleasure from experiences fades more slowly
Experiences are always cheaper than products
Experiences can be resold later at a profit
Products require too much storage at home
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the joy of a purchase fades fast, while memories and skills keep giving.

questions.q: Why might renting beat buying a home, according to the summary?
a: Fees, taxes and upkeep can erase most of the gain
Rent is always lower than a mortgage payment
Homes rarely rise in value over time
Landlords must cover every repair cost
questions.why: Lesson 3 says buying and selling costs, taxes and maintenance leave only a small profit.

questions.q: What does Shen say early retirement really depends on?
a: Keeping as much of what you earn as you can
Earning a six-figure salary every year
Picking individual stocks skilfully
Buying property before age thirty
questions.why: Lesson 3 stresses that the amount you keep, not the amount you earn, drives early retirement.
